claims.text: The premelting and melting behavior of Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles is governed by an interplay of chemical complexity, nanoscale phase-transition behavior, and varied configurations.
In situ characterization combined with molecular-dynamics simulations can reveal the governing physics of this premelting and melting behavior.
Chemical complexity and nanoscale phase-transition behavior lead to varied nanoparticle configurations.
The varied nanoparticle configurations influence premelting and melting behavior.
Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles will have a melting point 20% lower than that of baseline pure-iron nanoparticles.
Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles will have a premelting temperature range 10% greater than that of baseline pure-iron nanoparticles.
The proposed hypothesis applies to nanoparticles between 10 and 50 nm in size.
The exact interplay among chemical complexity, nanoscale phase-transition behavior, and varied configurations remains unclear.
A melting-point deviation greater than 5% from the predicted value falsifies the hypothesis.
A premelting-range deviation greater than 10% from the predicted value falsifies the hypothesis.
